bib.title: Don't Decay the Learning Rate, Increase the Batch Size

question: Can the benefits of decaying the learning rate be obtained by instead increasing the batch size during training, cutting parameter updates?
hypothesis: Decaying the learning rate acts by decaying the SGD noise scale g = eps(N/B - 1); raising B at constant eps should give the same learning curve per epoch with fewer updates.
contributions: Show empirically that decaying learning rate schedules convert directly into increasing batch size schedules with the same epochs and near-identical curves, for SGD, momentum, Nesterov and Adam
Further cut updates by raising learning rate (B proportional to eps) and momentum (B proportional to 1/(1-m))
Train Inception-ResNet-V2 on ImageNet in under 2500 updates with batches of 65536 and ResNet-50 to 76.1% in under 30 minutes on TPU, with no hyper-parameter tuning

method.summary: Existing step-decay schedules are converted so that when the learning rate would drop by factor alpha, the batch size grows by alpha instead (until a maximum batch size, after which the learning rate decays). Tested on CIFAR-10 wide ResNet and ImageNet with Inception-ResNet-V2 and ResNet-50.
method.task: image classification training schedule study (CIFAR-10, ImageNet)

models.name: Wide ResNet 16-4
models.architecture: wide ResNet (Zagoruyko & Komodakis 2016) with ghost batch norm, ghost batch 128

training.optimizer: SGD, SGD with momentum (0.9), Nesterov momentum (0.9), Adam (TensorFlow defaults, base lr 1e-3, beta1 0.9, beta2 0.999); ImageNet runs use momentum 0.9 to 0.9875
training.lr_schedule: step: noise scale divided by 5 in three steps on CIFAR (lr/5 per step, or B x5 per step); ImageNet divides noise scale by 10 at epochs 30, 60, 80 (B x10 until Bmax, then lr decay)
training.warmup: none for ImageNet Inception-ResNet-V2 (Goyal et al. used warm-up)
training.batch_size: CIFAR: 128 initial (640 or 3200 in larger-lr runs), Bmax 5120; ImageNet: 8192, 16384 or 32768 initial, Bmax 65536 (81920 in the Fig 6 run)
training.steps: CIFAR original ~80000 updates; ImageNet ~14000 baseline, under 2500 at best
training.epochs: 90 on ImageNet; CIFAR epoch count not stated
training.hardware: half TPU pod, 256 tensorcores (ResNet-50 run); distributed GPUs of batch size 64 (Inception-ResNet-V2)
training.wall_clock: ResNet-50: under 45 min at B=8192, under 30 min with B=16384 after epoch 30
training.seeds: CIFAR: 5 additional runs per schedule (median reported); ImageNet: 2 runs per schedule

other.noise_scale: g = eps(N/B - 1) ~ eps N/B; with momentum g ~ eps N/(B(1-m))
other.lost_epochs: N_lost = B/(N(1-m)) epochs lost to accumulation growth-in

metrics.name: parameter updates
metrics.definition: number of optimizer steps to finish training

baselines: Decaying learning rate with constant batch size (original schedules, Zagoruyko & Komodakis 2016; Goyal et al. 2017)
eval.protocol: Fixed number of epochs per schedule; curves compared by epochs and updates; medians over 5 runs on CIFAR, 2 runs on ImageNet; no significance tests

evidence.quote: We also train for 90 epochs and follow the same schedule

results.claim: Replacing lr decay by batch size increase on CIFAR-10 gives the same accuracy with far fewer updates: original schedule vs increasing batch size
results.setup: Wide ResNet 16-4 CIFAR-10, SGD momentum 0.9, B 128 x5 per step, lr 0.1 constant
results.quote: "Increasing batch size” requires ∼29000 updates, reaching a ﬁnal accuracy of 94.4%.

results.claim: Increased initial lr 0.5 with B 640 needs under 6500 updates
results.quote: “Increased initial learning rate” requires under 6500 updates, reaching a ﬁnal accuracy of 94.5%.

results.claim: Momentum 0.98 with B 3200 needs under 2500 updates but loses accuracy
results.quote: requires less than 2500 parameter updates, but reaches a lower test accuracy of 93.3%
results.note: Median over 5 extra runs 93.5% vs 94.3/94.2/94.2 for others

results.claim: Inception-ResNet-V2 on ImageNet: batch increase cuts updates from ~14000 to below 6000 with similar accuracy
results.setup: ImageNet, 90 epochs, lr 3.0, momentum 0.9, B 8192 -> 81920 at first step
results.quote: Increasing the batch size reduces the number of parameter updates during training from just over 14000 to below 6000.
results.note: Final acc: decay 78.7/77.8; batch increase 78.1/76.8 (two runs each)

results.claim: Momentum 0.9, initial B 8192, Bmax 65536 reaches 78.8% in just under 6000 updates
results.quote: “Momentum 0.9” achieves a ﬁnal accuracy of 78.8% in just under 6000 updates.

results.claim: Momentum 0.975, initial B 32768 or 16384, gets 77.5% and 76.8% in under 2500 updates
results.quote: Finally “Momentum 0.975” achieves ﬁnal accuracies of 77.5% and 76.8% in under 2500 updates.
results.note: Text says initial B 32768 for 'Momentum 0.9875' but results paragraph names 'Momentum 0.95' and 'Momentum 0.975'; labels inconsistent

results.claim: ResNet-50 reaches 76.1% in under 30 minutes by doubling batch to 16384 after epoch 30
results.setup: ImageNet, half TPU pod 256 tensorcores, 90 epochs, Goyal et al. setup
results.quote: and achieve the same validation accuracy of 76.1% in under 30 minutes

results.claim: Doubling initial lr with B=16384 throughout gives lower accuracy, showing batch growth matters
results.quote: achieves a lower validation set accuracy of 75.0% in 22 minutes

results.claim: Lost epochs from momentum accumulation grow-in: N_lost = B/(N(1-m))
results.setup: SGD with momentum, constant gradient assumption

results.claim: Test accuracy falls for initial learning rates above ~0.4 at constant batch size
results.setup: Wide ResNet CIFAR-10, B scaled proportional to lr, median of 5 runs
results.quote: We ﬁnd that the test accuracy falls for initial learning rates larger than ∼0.4.

limits: Scaling rules need B << N, so a Bmax is imposed (5120 on CIFAR, 65536 on ImageNet) after which lr decays again
Raising momentum with B proportional to 1/(1-m) lowers test accuracy slightly (93.3% vs 94.3% on CIFAR; 76.8-77.5% vs 78.8% on ImageNet)
Authors could not replicate the original paper's 95% CIFAR accuracy (got 94.3%)
Only image classification with step schedules; no language models, no cosine or other schedules tested; ImageNet runs only two seeds, with differences comparable to run-to-run variance
Test set evaluations were reduced for ImageNet, making curves noisy
Convex analysis (Sec 2) is mostly motivation; noise-scale argument rests on Smith & Le (2017)

terms.definition: g = eps(N/B - 1), the scale of random fluctuations in SGD dynamics; with momentum g = eps/(1-m) (N/B - 1)
batch norm computed on sub-batches of fixed size (Hoffer et al. 2017), so mean gradient is independent of batch size
